onboardedEditors.biography: Prof. Francis Verpoort, Chair Professor, State Key Laboratory of Advanced Technology for Material Synthesis and Processing, Wuhan University of Technology, China Professor Joint Institute of Chemical Research (FFMiEN), Peoples Friendship University of Russia (RUDN University), Moscow, Russia Prof. Francis Verpoort is a distinguished expert in organometallic chemistry and functional materials. He leads the Laboratory of Functional Hybrid Materials at Wuhan University of Technology and is the founder and CEO of SAIS Ltd, a company specializing in chemistry, materials, and engineering solutions. In addition to his research, Prof. Verpoort plays an active role in scientific publishing. He serves as the Editor of Applied Organometallic Chemistry, Editor-in-Chief of Chemistry Africa and Nanocatalysis, and is a member of the editorial boards of several other prestigious journals. His research focuses on organometallic chemistry, Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs), and Porous-Organic Polymers, with applications in catalysis, clean energy, and CO₂ capture. He has received numerous prestigious accolades, including the Dr. Basudev Banerjee Memorial Award and the “Chime” Award from Hubei Province, China. He also holds fellowships from the Royal Society of Chemistry, the Indian Chemical Society, and the International Engineering and Technology Institute. Prof. Francis Verpoort serves as Director General of the World Industrial Technology Organization (WITO), a global non-profit platform dedicated to advancing industrial technology innovation, cross-sector collaboration, and sustainable development worldwide. In 2025, he was also elected as Jury Chair of the International Expert Council of the Palladium Global Science Award (PGSA) In recognition of his outstanding contributions to science and technology, Prof. Verpoort has been elected as a member of the European Academy of Sciences and Arts, the Russian Academy of Natural Sciences, and the Mexican Academy of Sciences. Additionally, he has been designated a "National Distinguished Expert" in the People’s Republic of China.

onboardedEditors.biography:
Assoc. Prof. Dr. Aboubakr Haredi Abdelmonsef Ahmed is an Associate Professor of Organic Chemistry in the Chemistry Department, Faculty of Science, Qena University (formerly South Valley University), Qena, Egypt. With over 20 years of academic teaching, scientific leadership, and research mentorship, he has established an internationally recognized research portfolio at the intersection of organic synthetic chemistry, computational chemistry, and rational drug discovery.

He earned his Bachelor of Science in Chemistry with top honors from South Valley University in 2004, followed by a Master of Science in Organic Chemistry in 2010 focusing on the synthesis of biologically active quinazolinedione derivatives via Lossen rearrangement. In 2017, he received his Doctor of Philosophy in Chemistry from Osmania University (Hyderabad, India), where his doctoral investigations pioneered molecular modeling methodologies to identify novel lead inhibitors targeting Rab family GTPases. He has also undertaken distinguished international scientific missions, including research fellowship appointments at Jacobs University in Bremen, Germany.

Dr. Abdelmonsef's core research specializations encompass Organic and Heterocyclic Chemistry, Computer-Aided Drug Design (CADD), Bioinformatics, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics simulations, and In Silico Virtual Screening. His laboratory focuses on the rational design, green synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel nitrogen- and sulfur-heterocyclic scaffolds—notably quinazolin-2,4-diones, pyrazoles, thiazoles, triazoles, and fused heterocycles—as potent candidates against cancer targets (EGFR, VEGFR-2, c-Met, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, Aurora B kinase), multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens (MSSA, MRSA, VRSA), viral proteases, and inflammatory pathways.

His academic achievements include authoring over 75 peer-reviewed publications in prestigious international journals, publishing a dedicated academic monograph on heterocyclic synthesis, and securing competitive national grants such as the Academy of Scientific Research and Technology (ASRT) grant under the Nawah Scientific Center Alliance (2025). He is the recipient of the University Incentive Award in Basic and Engineering Sciences (2025) and multiple Scientific Publishing Awards. He has supervised and refereed more than 15 Ph.D. and M.Sc. theses and actively serves as an editorial board member and peer reviewer for numerous leading journals across the chemical, medicinal, and pharmacological sciences.
